audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is block RLP size validated before any processing occurs (EIP-7934)?

phase1_findings.implementation_notes: EIP-7934 block size validation is implemented in ValidateSuggestedBlock. The check occurs BEFORE transaction validation, using spec.IsEip7934Enabled flag and spec.Eip7934MaxRlpBlockSize limit.

phase2_findings.notes: The validation uses the pre-computed EncodedSize if available, otherwise calculates via RLP decoder. This ensures the check is performed efficiently before expensive operations.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Are blocks with non-empty ommers rejected in post-merge Ethereum?
audit_items.code_excerpt:
bool valid = !IsPostMerge ||
    ValidateHeaderField(header, header.Difficulty, UInt256.Zero, nameof(header.Difficulty))
    && ValidateHeaderField(header, header.Nonce, 0u, nameof(header.Nonce))
    && ValidateHeaderField(header, header.UnclesHash, Keccak.OfAnEmptySequenceRlp, nameof(header.UnclesHash));

phase1_findings.implementation_notes: Post-merge validation in MergeHeaderValidator checks that UnclesHash equals Keccak.OfAnEmptySequenceRlp (empty ommer hash). Non-empty ommers would fail this check.

phase2_findings.notes: The check is conditional on IsPostMerge flag from PoSSwitcher. Additionally, BlockValidator.cs line 75-81 limits uncle count via spec.MaximumUncleCount.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Do all 8 computed roots/hashes match header values after block execution?
audit_items.code_excerpt: Validates: GasUsed, Bloom, ReceiptsRoot, StateRoot, BlobGasUsed, ExcessBlobGas, ParentBeaconBlockRoot, RequestsHash

phase1_findings.implementation_notes: ValidateProcessedBlock compares processedBlock.Header.Hash with suggestedBlock.Header.Hash. On mismatch, detailed field-by-field comparison identifies the discrepancy for: GasUsed, Bloom, ReceiptsRoot, StateRoot, BlobGasUsed, ExcessBlobGas, ParentBeaconBlockRoot, RequestsHash.

phase2_findings.notes: All 8 fields from the spec are validated. The comparison is done at the end of block processing in BlockProcessor.ProcessOne.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is transaction sender identity correctly derived from ECDSA signature?

phase1_findings.implementation_notes: BaseSignatureTxValidator validates ECDSA signature parameters. EIP-2 malleable signature check (high-s rejection) is implemented via Secp256K1Curve.HalfNPlusOne comparison. R and S boundary checks prevent invalid curve points.

phase2_findings.notes: Legacy and typed transactions have separate validators (LegacySignatureTxValidator, SignatureTxValidator) both extending BaseSignatureTxValidator. Chain ID validation differs by transaction type.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is RLP encoding deterministic and collision-free?
audit_items.code_excerpt: SPECIFICATION-LEVEL: RLP encoding is handled by Nethermind.Serialization.Rlp library with deterministic encoders for each type.

phase1_findings.implementation_notes: RLP serialization uses dedicated decoder classes (BlockDecoder, HeaderDecoder, TransactionDecoder) that produce deterministic output. The library follows Ethereum RLP specification.

phase2_findings.notes: RLP encoding is a well-tested library component. Determinism is ensured by fixed encoding rules per type. Cross-implementation compatibility is verified by Ethereum execution spec tests.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is keccak256 collision-resistant and correctly implemented?
audit_items.code_excerpt: SPECIFICATION-LEVEL: Keccak256 implementation uses well-tested cryptographic library.

phase1_findings.implementation_notes: Nethermind uses standard Keccak256 implementation. Hash comparisons use constant-time equality via Hash256 type.

phase2_findings.notes: Cryptographic hash implementation is a foundational library component tested against standard test vectors.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is withdrawal amount scaled correctly by 10^9 (Gwei to Wei)?
audit_items.code_excerpt:
// Consensus clients are using Gwei for withdrawals amount. We need to convert it to Wei before applying state changes
_stateProvider.AddToBalanceAndCreateIfNotExists(withdrawal.Address, withdrawal.AmountInWei, spec);

phase1_findings.implementation_notes: WithdrawalProcessor uses withdrawal.AmountInWei property which performs the Gwei-to-Wei conversion. The comment explicitly documents this conversion.

phase2_findings.notes: The AmountInWei property on Withdrawal type handles the 10^9 multiplication. Need to verify overflow protection in AmountInWei getter.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does withdrawal processing only increase balances, never decrease?
audit_items.code_excerpt: _stateProvider.AddToBalanceAndCreateIfNotExists(withdrawal.Address, withdrawal.AmountInWei, spec);

phase1_findings.implementation_notes: ProcessWithdrawals only calls AddToBalanceAndCreateIfNotExists, which is an additive operation. No SubtractFromBalance calls exist in this method.

phase2_findings.notes: The method is simple and only performs balance additions. UInt256 type used for balances prevents underflow.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Do system contracts contain code before checked system transactions execute?

phase1_findings.implementation_notes: ReadRequests checks state.HasCode(contractAddress) before executing system transactions for withdrawal and consolidation requests. Throws InvalidBlockException if contract is empty.

phase2_findings.notes: This check is applied to WITHDRAWAL_REQUEST_ADDRESS and CONSOLIDATION_REQUEST_ADDRESS. Deposit requests are parsed from logs, not system calls.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Are checked system transaction errors propagated as InvalidBlock?

phase1_findings.implementation_notes: After executing system transactions via _transactionProcessor.Execute(), the tracer.StatusCode is checked. Failure status throws InvalidBlockException with appropriate error message.

phase2_findings.notes: Both WithdrawalsContractFailed and ConsolidationsContractFailed errors are handled distinctly. The check cannot be bypassed.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Are unchecked system transactions only used for beacon roots and history storage?
audit_items.code_excerpt: Beacon root storage in BeaconBlockRootHandler does not throw on failure, per EIP-4788 design.

phase1_findings.implementation_notes: BeaconBlockRootHandler.StoreBeaconRoot is called in BlockProcessor.StoreBeaconRoot wrapped in try-catch that only logs warnings on failure. History storage (EIP-2935) uses similar pattern in blockHashStore.ApplyBlockhashStateChanges.

phase2_findings.notes: The unchecked pattern is intentional for these operations as they affect ring buffer data only. Critical operations (withdrawals, consolidations) use checked pattern.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Do all blob versioned hashes have 0x01 version prefix?
audit_items.code_excerpt: case { Length: KzgPolynomialCommitments.BytesPerBlobVersionedHash } when transaction.BlobVersionedHashes[i][0] != KzgPolynomialCommitments.KzgBlobHashVersionV1: return TxErrorMessages.InvalidBlobVersionedHashVersion;

phase1_findings.implementation_notes: BlobFieldsTxValidator checks each versioned hash: validates length (BytesPerBlobVersionedHash) and first byte equals KzgBlobHashVersionV1 (0x01).

phase2_findings.notes: All versioned hashes in blob transactions are validated. Invalid version prefix returns TxErrorMessages.InvalidBlobVersionedHashVersion.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is gas refund capped at gas_used // 5 (EIP-3529)?
audit_items.code_excerpt: SPECIFICATION-LEVEL: Gas refund cap implemented in EVM transaction processing.

phase1_findings.implementation_notes: Gas refund cap (EIP-3529) is implemented in the transaction processor. The refund is limited to gas_used / spec.RefundDivisor (5 post-London).

phase2_findings.notes: RefundDivisor is spec-dependent, allowing for proper handling across hard forks. Integer division ensures no overflow.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is EIP-7623 calldata floor gas cost enforced after refund?
audit_items.code_excerpt: SPECIFICATION-LEVEL: EIP-7623 calldata floor gas cost implemented in transaction processing.

phase1_findings.implementation_notes: EIP-7623 adds floor gas cost based on calldata. IntrinsicGasCalculator computes this floor, and the final gas_used takes the maximum of (execution_gas - refund) and calldata_floor.

phase2_findings.notes: The floor ensures minimum payment for calldata regardless of refunds from storage operations.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Are post-merge header fields (difficulty, nonce, ommers_hash) correctly zeroed?
audit_items.code_excerpt:
bool valid = !IsPostMerge ||
    ValidateHeaderField(header, header.Difficulty, UInt256.Zero, nameof(header.Difficulty))
    && ValidateHeaderField(header, header.Nonce, 0u, nameof(header.Nonce))
    && ValidateHeaderField(header, header.UnclesHash, Keccak.OfAnEmptySequenceRlp, nameof(header.UnclesHash));

phase1_findings.implementation_notes: MergeHeaderValidator.ValidateTheMergeChecks enforces: Difficulty = 0, Nonce = 0, UnclesHash = Keccak.OfAnEmptySequenceRlp for post-merge blocks.

phase2_findings.notes: The check is applied only when IsPostMerge is true, determined by PoSSwitcher based on TTD.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Are sender accounts with code validated for EIP-7702 delegation designations?
audit_items.code_excerpt:
RegisterValidator(TxType.SetCode, new CompositeTxValidator([
    new ReleaseSpecTxValidator(static spec => spec.IsEip7702Enabled),
    IntrinsicGasTxValidator.Instance,
    SignatureTxValidator.Instance,
    expectedChainIdTxValidator,
    GasFieldsTxValidator.Instance,
    ContractSizeTxValidator.Instance,
    NonBlobFieldsTxValidator.Instance,
    NoContractCreationTxValidator.Instance,
    AuthorizationListTxValidator.Instance,
    GasLimitCapTxValidator.Instance
]));

phase1_findings.implementation_notes: SetCode (EIP-7702) transactions have dedicated validators including AuthorizationListTxValidator. Sender account code check for delegation designation would be in transaction execution context.

phase2_findings.notes: The validation ensures authorization lists are non-empty and transactions cannot create contracts. Full delegation designation validation happens during execution.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is transaction gas checked against remaining block gas?
audit_items.code_excerpt: SPECIFICATION-LEVEL: Transaction gas vs block gas limit check in transaction processor.

phase1_findings.implementation_notes: Transaction processor validates tx.GasLimit against remaining block gas before execution. The check ensures cumulative gas doesn't exceed block gas limit.

phase2_findings.notes: Block gas tracking is maintained throughout block processing. Transactions exceeding remaining gas are rejected.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is transaction blob gas checked against remaining block blob gas?

phase1_findings.implementation_notes: BlobFieldsTxValidator.ValidateBlobGasLimits checks transaction blob gas against spec.GetMaxBlobGasPerBlock(). Also checks per-tx limit via spec.GetMaxBlobGasPerTx().

phase2_findings.notes: Both per-transaction and per-block blob gas limits are enforced. BlockValidator.ValidateEip4844Fields also performs cumulative block-level blob gas validation.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is max_fee_per_gas >= max_priority_fee_per_gas enforced for EIP-1559 transactions?
audit_items.code_excerpt:
public ValidationResult IsWellFormed(Transaction transaction, IReleaseSpec releaseSpec) =>
    transaction.MaxFeePerGas < transaction.MaxPriorityFeePerGas ? TxErrorMessages.InvalidMaxPriorityFeePerGas : ValidationResult.Success;

phase1_findings.implementation_notes: GasFieldsTxValidator explicitly checks MaxFeePerGas >= MaxPriorityFeePerGas. Returns InvalidMaxPriorityFeePerGas error on violation.

phase2_findings.notes: Applied to EIP-1559, Blob, and SetCode transaction types via CompositeTxValidator.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is max_fee_per_gas >= base_fee_per_gas enforced?

phase1_findings.implementation_notes: BlockValidator.ValidateEip4844Fields checks MaxFeePerBlobGas against calculated feePerBlobGas. For regular gas, the check is in transaction processor during execution context.

phase2_findings.notes: The base fee comparison happens at block validation time with current block's base fee.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Do blob transactions have between 1 and BLOB_COUNT_LIMIT blobs?

phase1_findings.implementation_notes: ValidateBlobGasLimits checks txBlobCount >= MinBlobsPerTransaction (1) and calculates blob gas to compare against max limits. Both lower and upper bounds enforced.

phase2_findings.notes: Zero blobs rejected with BlobTxMissingBlobs. Excess blobs rejected via blob gas calculations against per-tx and per-block limits.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Are blob and SetCode transactions prevented from creating contracts?

phase1_findings.implementation_notes: BlobFieldsTxValidator returns TxMissingTo when To is null. SetCode validator uses NoContractCreationTxValidator which checks IsContractCreation flag.

phase2_findings.notes: Both transaction types explicitly prevent contract creation through dedicated validators in their composite validator chains.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Do SetCode transactions require non-empty authorization lists?

phase1_findings.implementation_notes: AuthorizationListTxValidator rejects transactions with null or empty (Length: 0) authorization lists via MissingAuthorizationList error.

phase2_findings.notes: Both null and empty array cases are handled. This validator is part of SetCode transaction's CompositeTxValidator.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does sender nonce match transaction nonce exactly?
audit_items.code_excerpt: SPECIFICATION-LEVEL: Nonce validation in transaction processor before execution.

phase1_findings.implementation_notes: Transaction processor validates exact nonce match: tx.Nonce must equal sender account nonce. Both higher and lower nonces are rejected.

phase2_findings.notes: Nonce validation prevents replay attacks and ensures transaction ordering within the same account.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is sender balance sufficient for maximum possible transaction cost?
audit_items.code_excerpt: SPECIFICATION-LEVEL: Balance check includes (tx.gas * max_fee_per_gas) + tx.value + blob_gas_fee.

phase1_findings.implementation_notes: Transaction processor validates sender balance covers maximum cost: GasLimit * MaxFeePerGas + Value + (BlobGas * MaxFeePerBlobGas for blob txs).

phase2_findings.notes: UInt256 arithmetic prevents overflow. Balance is checked before any state modifications.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is nonce incremented before message execution?
audit_items.code_excerpt: SPECIFICATION-LEVEL: Nonce increment happens before EVM execution begins.

phase1_findings.implementation_notes: Transaction processor increments sender nonce immediately after validation checks, before calling into EVM for message execution.

phase2_findings.notes: Early nonce increment prevents reentrancy-based nonce reuse attacks within the same transaction.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Are gas fees deducted from sender balance before message execution?
audit_items.code_excerpt: SPECIFICATION-LEVEL: Gas fees deducted upfront before EVM execution.

phase1_findings.implementation_notes: Transaction processor deducts maximum gas cost (GasLimit * effective_gas_price) and blob gas fees from sender before EVM execution.

phase2_findings.notes: Upfront deduction prevents sender from spending reserved gas fees during execution.

audit_items.title: Is unused gas refunded at the correct effective_gas_price?
audit_items.code_excerpt: SPECIFICATION-LEVEL: Refund calculation uses effective_gas_price, not max_fee.

phase1_findings.implementation_notes: After execution, unused gas (gas_left) is refunded at effective_gas_price (min(max_fee, base_fee + priority_fee)).

phase2_findings.notes: The refund uses the same effective_gas_price as the initial deduction, ensuring correct accounting.

audit_items.title: Does coinbase receive only the priority fee portion (not base fee)?
audit_items.code_excerpt: SPECIFICATION-LEVEL: Coinbase payment = gas_used * (effective_gas_price - base_fee).

phase1_findings.implementation_notes: Transaction processor pays coinbase the priority fee portion only. Base fee is burned (not credited to any account) per EIP-1559.

phase2_findings.notes: EIP-1559 deflationary mechanism correctly implemented - base fee is effectively removed from circulation.

audit_items.title: Are accounts marked for deletion destroyed after transaction execution?
audit_items.code_excerpt: SPECIFICATION-LEVEL: SELFDESTRUCT queues accounts for deletion, processed post-execution.

phase1_findings.implementation_notes: SELFDESTRUCT opcode marks accounts for deletion. These are processed after transaction execution, with balance transfer to beneficiary.

phase2_findings.notes: Post-Cancun, SELFDESTRUCT behavior is modified (EIP-6780) - only deletes in same-transaction-created contracts.

audit_items.title: Does beacon roots system transaction execute before user transactions?

phase1_findings.implementation_notes: ProcessBlock calls StoreBeaconRoot (EIP-4788) BEFORE ProcessTransactions. The ordering is explicit in the code.

phase2_findings.notes: Beacon root is stored first, then block hash store is updated, then state is committed, then user transactions process.

audit_items.title: Does history storage system transaction execute as second operation?
audit_items.code_excerpt: blockHashStore.ApplyBlockhashStateChanges(header, spec);

phase1_findings.implementation_notes: ApplyBlockhashStateChanges (EIP-2935 history storage) is called after StoreBeaconRoot and before ProcessTransactions.

phase2_findings.notes: The ordering is: 1) beacon root, 2) block hash store, 3) commit, 4) user transactions.

audit_items.title: Are transactions processed in sequential order within a block?
audit_items.code_excerpt: SPECIFICATION-LEVEL: Transactions processed sequentially in block order.

phase1_findings.implementation_notes: BlockTransactionsExecutor.ProcessTransactions iterates through block.Transactions array sequentially, maintaining deterministic ordering.

phase2_findings.notes: Sequential processing is fundamental for consensus. No parallelization that could violate ordering.

audit_items.title: Are withdrawals processed after all transactions?
audit_items.code_excerpt: withdrawalProcessor.ProcessWithdrawals(block, spec);

phase1_findings.implementation_notes: ProcessWithdrawals is called AFTER ProcessTransactions completes and miner rewards are applied.

phase2_findings.notes: Ordering in ProcessBlock: transactions -> miner rewards -> withdrawals -> execution requests.

audit_items.title: Are general purpose requests processed last in block body?
audit_items.code_excerpt: executionRequestsProcessor.ProcessExecutionRequests(block, _stateProvider, receipts, spec);

phase1_findings.implementation_notes: ProcessExecutionRequests is called after ProcessWithdrawals, making it the last major operation before final state commit.

phase2_findings.notes: The final ordering: withdrawals -> commit -> execution requests -> end block trace -> final commit.

audit_items.title: Are request types appended in correct order (deposits, withdrawals, consolidations)?

phase1_findings.implementation_notes: ProcessExecutionRequests adds to requests array in order: 1) ProcessDeposits, 2) Withdrawal requests, 3) Consolidation requests.

phase2_findings.notes: The order matches EIP-6110, EIP-7002, EIP-7251 specification requirements.

audit_items.title: Are deposit requests parsed from block output logs (not system transactions)?

phase1_findings.implementation_notes: ProcessDeposits iterates through transaction receipts' logs, filtering for DepositContractAddress and DepositEvent topic. No system transaction is involved.

phase2_findings.notes: Deposits are parsed from logs, not system calls. ABI decoding validates deposit event structure.

audit_items.title: Are withdrawal and consolidation requests from checked system transactions?

phase1_findings.implementation_notes: ReadRequests executes system transactions for withdrawal and consolidation contracts. Both HasCode check and execution failure check throw InvalidBlockException.

phase2_findings.notes: This is the 'checked' system transaction pattern - failures cause block rejection unlike beacon root (unchecked).

audit_items.title: Are blocks with number < 1 rejected?

phase1_findings.implementation_notes: ValidateParent allows Number=0 only for genesis block (parent is null). ValidateFieldLimit also rejects negative block numbers.

phase2_findings.notes: Block 0 is only valid as genesis. Non-genesis blocks require parent with Number = child.Number - 1.

audit_items.title: Are block timestamps strictly increasing?

phase1_findings.implementation_notes: ValidateTimestamp enforces strict inequality: header.Timestamp > parent.Timestamp. Equal timestamps are rejected.

phase2_findings.notes: Strictly greater comparison ensures time always moves forward.

audit_items.title: Are block numbers sequential (parent.number + 1)?

phase1_findings.implementation_notes: ValidateBlockNumber enforces exact sequential increment: header.Number must equal parent.Number + 1.

phase2_findings.notes: Both gaps and duplicates are rejected by this check.

audit_items.title: Does parent_hash cryptographically match parent header?

phase1_findings.implementation_notes: ValidateParent checks header.ParentHash matches parent.Hash. Parent header hash is computed via keccak256(rlp(header)).

phase2_findings.notes: The comparison uses Hash256 equality which is cryptographically sound.

audit_items.title: Does excess_blob_gas match calculation from parent?

phase1_findings.implementation_notes: ValidateBlobGasFields calculates expected excess blob gas from parent header and compares to header.ExcessBlobGas.

phase2_findings.notes: BlobGasCalculator.CalculateExcessBlobGas implements the EIP-4844 excess blob gas formula.

audit_items.title: Is gas_used <= gas_limit enforced in header?

phase1_findings.implementation_notes: ValidateGasUsed checks header.GasUsed <= header.GasLimit. Violation returns ExceededGasLimit error.

phase2_findings.notes: Simple bounds check with clear error reporting.

audit_items.title: Do system transactions originate from SYSTEM_ADDRESS (0xff...fe)?
audit_items.code_excerpt: SenderAddress = Address.SystemUser,  // 0xfffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffe

phase1_findings.implementation_notes: System transactions (_withdrawalTransaction, _consolidationTransaction) have SenderAddress = Address.SystemUser (0xfffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffe).

phase2_findings.notes: Address.SystemUser is defined as constant 0xfffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffe in Address.cs.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does base fee calculation enforce minimum increase of 1 when gas exceeds target?

phase1_findings.implementation_notes: DefaultBaseFeeCalculator uses UInt256.Max(..., UInt256.One) to ensure minimum increase of 1 when gas exceeds target.

phase2_findings.notes: The minimum of 1 prevents base fee from staying stagnant when demand exceeds target.

audit_items.title: Verify transaction validation check ordering: Are checks ordered from general to specific?
audit_items.code_excerpt: Validators ordered: ReleaseSpec -> IntrinsicGas -> Signature -> ChainId -> GasFields -> ContractSize -> BlobFields -> Authorization

phase1_findings.implementation_notes: CompositeTxValidator runs validators in registration order. Cheap checks (type, spec version) precede expensive ones (signature, intrinsic gas).

phase2_findings.notes: Ordering is reasonable for DoS prevention - type check first, then signature validation.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is extra_data in block header limited to 32 bytes?

phase1_findings.implementation_notes: MergeHeaderValidator.ValidateExtraData checks ExtraData.Length <= 32 for post-merge blocks. Pre-merge uses spec.MaximumExtraDataSize.

phase2_findings.notes: Post-merge hard-codes 32 bytes per EIP-3675. Pre-merge limit is configurable via spec.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is gas limit change bounded by parent_gas_limit // 1024?

phase1_findings.implementation_notes: ValidateGasLimitRange calculates maxGasLimitDifference = parentGasLimit / GasLimitBoundDivisor (1024). Both upper and lower bounds checked.

phase2_findings.notes: Handles overflow edge case for very high gas limits (long.MaxValue in hive tests).

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is gas limit >= 5000 (GAS_LIMIT_MINIMUM) enforced?
audit_items.code_excerpt:
bool gasLimitNotTooLow = header.GasLimit > adjustedParentGasLimit - maxGasLimitDifference &&
                         header.GasLimit >= spec.MinGasLimit;

phase1_findings.implementation_notes: ValidateGasLimitRange enforces header.GasLimit >= spec.MinGasLimit. MinGasLimit is typically 5000 per Ethereum spec.

phase2_findings.notes: Minimum gas limit is spec-dependent, allowing for chain-specific configurations.
